{"text":"The current graph has enclosing 囗 strokes around inner strokes; this modern description does not establish the ancient identities or roles of those shapes. Ancient analyses remain disputed. One interprets four horizontal marks as counting rods representing four; 字源 describes the separate graph 亖 as a direct numeral. Another proposes that 四 was a graph for 呬 depicting breath, later reused for ‘four’ because of sound similarity; the proposed breath-related referent’s original name is not independently established. A separate proposal treats 四 as the original graph of 泗, depicting nasal discharge, then borrowed for ‘four’; this proposal lacks textual attestation. Neither borrowing account is established.","evidence_ids":["ref018","ref027","ref033","ref034","ref040","ref041","ref045","ref049","ref051","ref052"]}
